description: Hi, I’m Pratima Guragain, a graduate student pursuing my Master of Architecture. I started out with vibe coding this summer, and I’m always looking to expand my horizons and try new things. I’m strongest at visual design, layout, and making complex information easy to read.
summary: I developed Bhu Cycle, a platform farmers can use to make better-informed decisions about crop rotation. It keeps them connected to their community and up to date on what others around them are growing. It also gives them sustainable, natural ways to deal with insects, in place of insecticides that harm the soil. The platform also addresses soil pollution and the lack of information that farming communities face, especially in rural areas. This could also be a first step in introducing students and the next generation to farming, in a way that is easy to understand.
details:
Bhu Cycle is decision-making support for farmers. Bhu means earth and soil, and the cycle is how each crop shapes the next one

How does it work?

  • The farmer enters their location. For now, the project covers Lincoln, Illinois.
  • The system pulls NASA POWER data for that place: temperature, rainfall and soil moisture.
  • It analyzes the last 30 days against the long-term averages and shows current conditions in three groups (Soil, Temperature and Rain), each with a short note such as “drier than usual.”
  • Crop icons sit below the conditions. Tapping one shows what that crop does to the soil.
  • To plan the next planting, the farmer says when they sowed their last crop, what it was, and the season they want to plant in.
  • The system takes the NASA data and the last crop into consideration and recommends crops that fit.
  • Selecting a crop shows what happens if it is planted: how it follows the last crop, what it does to the soil, the weather it will grow through, and whether rainfall usually covers its water needs.
  • The farmer can enter their plot size to get an estimate of the seed they need.
  • A natural remedies section gives home remedies for common pest problems, as an alternative to chemical insecticides.

What benefits does it have?

  • NASA holds years of data on growing conditions, but it is hard for a farmer to read in the form it comes in. Bhu Cycle makes that data more readable.
  • Farmers can see the effect of a crop choice before they plant.
  • Natural remedies give farmers a lower-chemical option for common pests.
  • We want Bhu Cycle to grow into a database of what farmers plant, and a platform where farmers nearby can connect and help each other out. The connect feature is part of the design and is not built yet.

The ideas behind this project are all mine. I used Claude Code only to build it. I am an architecture graduate student, and problem solving is what I have been trained in throughout my undergraduate and graduate studies. Coding is not. I started vibe coding this summer, and I have been eager to learn more ever since.

This project is creative for me because it pushed me further into problem solving and critical thinking in daily life. It also made me think about problems around the world that are essential to address.
